# Verifying the result

How to check what you built, and the exceptions that make a naive check wrong. All of it runs against a
rendered page in a real browser — none of it is a code review, and the ones worth the most are the ones
axe does not report.

`tests/shared/a11y.spec.mjs` in this repo drives every check below over every component, and
`agents/testing.md` has the harness traps that come with writing them.

## The checks

**axe, with the WCAG tags, and nothing left unclaimed**

`new AxeBuilder({ page }).withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa',
'best-practice']).analyze()`. The cheapest check, and not a sufficient one — nothing else on this list
is something axe reports.

**Contrast, in every theme**

Contrast is the one check whose result depends on the token values rather than the markup, so it runs
once per theme in both modes. `withRules(['color-contrast'])` per theme is fast enough to repeat; a full
axe pass per theme is not.

**No positive `tabindex` anywhere**

The one thing that actually detaches tab order from DOM order, which SC 2.4.3 requires to agree with
reading order. A roving tabindex moves between `0` and `-1` and never above.

**Every tab stop can really take focus**

Ask the browser rather than trusting a selector list: `el.focus({ preventScroll: true })`, then
`document.activeElement === el`. Restore focus afterward.

**Focus is visible on every tab stop**

SC 2.4.7. An `outline` with a width and a style that is not `none`, or a `box-shadow`. A component that
replaces the ring with something else has to say what.

**A focused control is never left under a sticky header**

SC 2.4.11. Focus the element with scrolling allowed, then compare its `getBoundingClientRect().top`
against the header's height. Scrolling *forward* aligns an element's bottom edge, so the header only
eats the element moving backwards — which means a check that only Tabs downward will never see it.

**Every pointer target clears 24×24**

SC 2.5.8, with the exceptions below. A pointer can hit the control or any label bound to it, so the
target clears the floor if any one of those boxes clears it in **both** dimensions. Comparing areas
instead picks a full-width block label, which is 282px wide and 18px tall and clears nothing.

**Reduced motion removes every duration, by both routes**

The media query is the OS preference and an attribute like `[data-motion="off"]` is the in-page control.
They are different mechanisms, and a component gated on only one of them looks correct until it is
tested against the other. Read `transitionDuration` and `animationDuration` off every element in the
subtree and require zero from both routes.

**The forced-colors block exists, and it takes effect**

Two halves, and the second is the one that matters: the string `@media (forced-colors: active)` is in
the stylesheet, *and* a snapshot of computed colors across the subtree changes when the media is
emulated. The first half alone passes for a block full of dead rules.

**Nothing overflows sideways at 320px**

SC 1.4.10 — 320px is 1280px at 400% zoom, which is what the criterion is really about.
`documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth` must be `<= 0`. This is where a fieldset's min-content
width, or one unbreakable token in a readout, shows up.

## The exceptions that make a naive check wrong

**Filter on `:disabled`, never on `el.disabled`**

The IDL property misses every control inside a `<fieldset disabled>`, and a disabled control is
correctly out of the tab order and correctly has no focus ring — so the sweep reports healthy markup as
broken.

**SC 2.5.8 exempts inline links and user-agent-sized controls**

It applies to *pointer* targets, so a focusable heading or scroll region is not one. A link inside a
sentence is sized by the line-height around it. A native checkbox or radio is drawn by the browser at
13–18px and the author has not touched it. A link *alone* in a paragraph gets no inline exception,
though — there is no surrounding sentence, so it is just a 16px target.

**A clipped control is not a pointer target in that state**

The visually-hidden skip-link recipe is 1×1 until it is revealed. Skip anything whose `clipPath` is not
`none`, and measure the revealed state separately.

**A live region cannot be asserted visible**

It is empty by definition until something lands in it, so it is 0px tall and a geometric visibility
check calls it hidden. Assert the negative instead. Any sweep that requires everything it finds to be
visible fails on every live region on the page.

**An element already on screen is not "obscured"**

The sticky-header check has to distinguish a control the browser actually scrolled to from one that was
comfortably in view already. Bound it on both sides: `top < headerHeight` **and** `top > -headerHeight`.

**Forced-colors emulation does not repaint author backgrounds**

So the assertion is "something changed", never "the tint is gone". Writing it the second way produces a
check that fails on a correct component.

## Deliberate failures

**An example that is broken on purpose has to say so, and has to stay broken**

Most component pages in this library ship one live failure, because a failure you can Tab into teaches
more than a paragraph about one. The failing element carries `data-ac-demo-broken="<check> <check>"`
naming what it is expected to fail — any axe rule id, plus `focus-visible` (SC 2.4.7) and `target-size`
(SC 2.5.8).

The sweep does not skip those. It asserts they **still** fail, so an example that quietly stops being
broken — a fix applied to the wrong copy, a good CSS rule that reached further than it was meant to —
fails the build as well. A violation inside a marked element that is *not* in its list is still a
failure, which is what keeps the claim honest. If you are copying out of this library, never copy from
inside one.
